name: R1_composite_core
hypothesis: A fixed, theory-signed equal-weight composite of quality (+gross profitability, +operating ROA), low accruals, value (+book-to-market), low volatility, 12-1 momentum and one-month reversal ranks next-90-day returns.  Nothing is fitted.

name: R2_composite_trend
hypothesis: Adding fundamental trend and financing signals with their published signs (+ROA change, +revenue growth, -asset growth, -net share issuance, +trailing earnings yield) improves the ranking (vs R1; only features change).

name: R3_ridge_12
hypothesis: Weights fitted by Ridge on past matured outcomes rank better than equal weights with fixed signs (vs R2; same 12 features, only the model changes).

name: R4_ridge_21
hypothesis: The remaining registered features (63-day return, distance from 52-week high, net margin, leverage, cash, free cash flow, filing age, size, liquidity) add information to the fitted model (vs R3; only features change).

name: R5_ridge_tuned_21
hypothesis: Choosing the Ridge penalty on the most recent slice of each fit's own training rows (candidates 1 to 10,000) beats the fixed penalty of 10 (vs R4; only the model changes).

name: P1_top50__R1
hypothesis: Holding 50 instead of 30 names per cohort diversifies stock-specific risk without diluting the signal much (vs the selected alpha's base; only n changes).

name: P2_top100__R1
hypothesis: Holding 100 names per cohort trades more of the signal's edge for diversification; tests whether the edge is concentrated in the very top ranks (vs base; only n changes).

name: P3_inverse_vol__R1
hypothesis: Weighting the same 30 names by inverse 63-day volatility lowers portfolio risk without giving up return (vs base; only the sizing rule changes).
